Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we can keep momentum on the procurement side: 

Summary of your requirements (as I understood them):
- Primary goal: run Redwood privately in AcmeHealth VPC with no cross-tenant data egress to public internet.
- Data types: PHI/PII examples include patient names, MRNs, and limited clinical notes. You flagged transcripts that contain PHI.
- Retention: you prefer a 30-day transient retention policy for inference-related logs, with longer-term audit logs (only metadata) retained for 12 months.
- Logging controls: ability to disable input logging, redact PII from logs, and export audit logs to your SIEM (Splunk).
- Network: VPC peering or PrivateLink, strict egress allowlists, and an on-prem/air-gapped option for final validation.

Attachments: I attached our suggested dataflow diagram for a Redwood Private deployment (private_vpc_dataflow_diagram.pdf) and the sample fields file you mentioned (acme_sample_data_fields.csv).

Requested clarifications / asks to move to technical review:
1) Can you confirm whether any of the data we will send to Redwood is stored on your side prior to inference (e.g., pre-processed logs)?
2) For the 30-day transient retention, do you need an API to purge inference content on demand, or is scheduled automatic purge acceptable?
3) Which team should we schedule the technical deep-dive with — Security, Network, or both? You mentioned Sofia and Kevin on the call.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the point above by end of day Thursday (4/16).
- Technical deep-dive w/ Redwood security & infra: propose Tue 4/21 10am PT. (Please confirm)

Looping in Monica (CS lead) to help with SLA/contract questions. I'll also add Nikhil (security) and Dev (platform) to the thread after your confirmation.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications inline: 

- We do pre-process transcripts (remove explicit PHI where possible) but we expect some residual PHI to make it to inference requests. So we need inference to happen inside our VPC and for Redwood to not persist plain-text inputs by default.
- 30-day transient retention is the goal but we would also like an on-demand purge API for any records flagged by our QA.
- For logging, we need the ability to disable verbatim input logging and only capture structured metadata (request id, model version, token counts). We will ship audit logs to our Splunk collector over a private connection.
- Network: we prefer PrivateLink but can consider VPC peering. For air-gapped validation we want an installer image or on-prem bundle for a staging environment.

We can do the technical deep-dive with Security + Network on Tue 4/21 10am PT — I'll send a calendar invite. For the deep-dive please have your infra and security engineers present.

- On-demand purge API: yes, Redwood Private exposes an admin endpoint to trigger purge of stored inference artifacts; we'll document auth and audit behavior in the deep-dive.

- Audit logs: we can forward structured audit events (no raw inputs) over a secure forwarder to your Splunk HEC endpoint inside the VPC.
- Network: Dev will outline PrivateLink and peering pros/cons. For on-prem/air-gapped: we have an appliance deployment option (air-gapped installer) but full air-gap requires a support engagement — we'll cover constraints in the deep-dive.

Hi Alex / team — Nikhil here from Redwood security. Per Marissa's request I pulled together the key points on encryption, logging, and key management for the deep dive. High level: 

1) Encryption & KMS
- We support BYOK via customer-managed KMS keys in your cloud account. Encryption at rest uses AES-256; envelope encryption is supported for added isolation.
- For HSM-style keys we integrate with cloud HSMs; we also support integration with on-prem HSMs over mutually-authenticated TLS where the deployment permits.

2) Logging / Data retention
- Default behavior for Redwood Private is to not persist raw inputs to disk unless explicitly enabled.
- Admins can configure per-route logging mode: "none", "metadata-only", or "full". For AcmeHealth we recommend "metadata-only".
- Purge API: authenticated endpoint that removes inference artifacts. Purge operations are logged (metadata only) and can be routed to your SIEM.
- Retention windows are configurable; we can enforce 30-day transient retention for inference artifacts and 12 months for metadata/audit logs.

3) Egress & network boundaries
- PrivateLink recommended: allows interface endpoints inside your VPC with no internet egress. We provide endpoint service config and recommendations for security groups/route tables.
- When peering is used, we recommend explicit deny rules for outgoing internet traffic at the subnet level and an egress proxy for allowed updates (signed images only).

4) Air-gapped / on-prem
- We offer an installer image for staging that runs in air-gapped environments. Full air-gap (no external connectivity) requires a RSA-signed image signing process and offline support bundle exchange. This is delivered under an enterprise support engagement.

I'll present these details and sample policies on Tue 4/21. In the meantime, attaching a short runbook and the KMS integration matrix.

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
